text: Refactoring is the process of improving the structure of your code without changing what it actually does. The goal is to make the code cleaner, easier to read, and simpler to maintain. For example, you might rename confusing variables, break a long function into smaller parts, or remove duplicated logic. Even though the program’s behavior stays exactly the same, the internal design becomes much better. This practice helps reduce “technical debt,” which is the extra work you create when you write messy code quickly. By regularly refactoring, you avoid future problems and make it easier for your team to understand and modify the code later.
